title: lynwood-health integration - call notes and action items
content:
Call: Lyndwood (Lynwood Health) integration kickoff - 2026-06-15
Attendees: Asha Patel (Redwood SE - owner), Mateo Ruiz (Redwood Dev), Priya Sharma (Redwood SRE), Liam O'Connor (Lynwood - Platform Lead), Sara Nguyen (Lynwood - Security), Dev Team x2 (Lynwood)
Duration: 45m

Context / goals:
- Lynwood wants to add LLM-powered triage and summarization for inbound patient messages (secure messaging) into their portal.
- Primary goals: latency <= 400ms p50 for short prompts (50-200 tokens), predictable cost, and HIPAA-aligned hosting (auditable logs, KMS).
- Start as Private deployment (VPC) with potential move to Dedicated in 6-12 months depending on volume.

High-level integration notes:
- API surface: Lynwood will call Redwood's Private endpoint via service-to-service auth. They prefer a gRPC-like interface but are ok starting with REST.
- Expected traffic: initial pilot ~500 requests/day, peak bursts up to ~250 req/min during clinic hours. Long term estimate 20k/day in 6 months if feature adopted.
- Input/Output: Patient messages (PII) will be sent; they require request/response not to be logged in plaintext in Redwood control plane. They want request encryption at rest with customer-managed KMS key.
- Models: prefer an open model (gpt-3.5-like equivalent) with quantization for cost. We'll propose a small-medium model family and fallbacks for quality.

Security & compliance:
- HIPAA: Lynwood needs BAAs and audit logs. They require Private deployment inside their AWS account (VPC) or Redwood-managed Private with strict log redaction and KMS integration.
- KMS: Must support their AWS KMS key (Customer managed). Confirmed KMS integration available in Redwood Private; need steps for key grant/rotate.
- Data residency: US-only.
- Logging: They require only hashed request ids in control plane logs; full payloads must be disabled or encrypted.
- Pen tests / IR: They will run a short security review; need an architecture doc + threat model before their security team signs off (linked in artifacts).

Performance & reliability:
- Latency SLO target: p50 <= 400ms, p95 <= 900ms for short prompts (note: includes network RTT to their VPC gateway).
- Throughput target: support bursts to 250 req/min with low queuing; autoscaling in Dedicated mode later.
- Caching: suggested prefix caching for common system prompts to reduce cost/latency. Discussed KV cache behavior for session-based conversation (they want session affinity).

Integration gotchas called out on call:
- Authentication: they currently use OIDC for service auth. Need a short-lived token exchange flow (we suggested Signed JWT with Redwood token exchange). Action: put short example (Asha).
- Redaction: their devs prefer redaction at client side before sending; security insisted on server-side policies. Need to map fields they consider PHI vs allowed metadata.
- Model governance: clinical phrasing needs guardrails to avoid giving medical advice. They will provide prompt templates and a small eval set. Need automatic quality monitoring and regression alerts (Redwood Optimize).
- VPC peering vs private endpoint: Decision pending. Peering easiest for them but easier to manage via Private deployment endpoints.

Open questions (to resolve):
- Can Redwood disable control-plane request bodies for Private? (Action: Priya to confirm with infra SRE)
- Exact KMS grant steps for cross-account key use (Action: Mateo to draft steps)
- Which model family to recommend for clinical summarization (Action: Asha + Devs to run a quick eval with 20 sample prompts)
- Tokenization accounting for templates vs patient text (affects cost estimates)

Immediate next steps / owners:
- Asha: Draft example request/response snippets (REST and JWT sign flow) and send to Lynwood by 2026-06-18. (linked ticket: JIRA-5782)
- Mateo: Write KMS cross-account grant checklist + minimal IAM policy by 2026-06-19.
- Priya: Confirm control-plane logging redaction capability and whether payloads can be disabled or encrypted; by 2026-06-20.
- Lynwood (Liam/Sara): Share 20 sample messages (anonymized) for quick eval and prompt tuning by 2026-06-18.
- Asha + Lynwood devs: Run an initial quality eval on 20 samples and pick a candidate model family by 2026-06-22.
- Create a Confluence security brief and architecture diagram for Lynwood security review (owner: Asha, due 2026-06-21).

Risks / blockers:
- Security sign-off timeline uncertain — could delay pilot >3 weeks.
- KMS cross-account complexity may require support from Lynwood infra team.
- Need to ensure prompt templates remove or obfuscate restricted PHI fields.

Notes / miscellaneous:
- Demo idea: prepare a small sandbox in our test Private environment showing redaction flow + KV-cached sessions. Good to include in next call.
- Lynwood indicated budget sensitivity — propose a cost estimate with quantized model to show delta between unquantized and quantized variants.

Follow-up call: propose 2026-06-23 (30m) to review artifacts and security doc. Asha to send invite once Confluence doc is ready.

Quick links:
- JIRA-5782: lynwood onboarding epic (owner: Asha)
- Confluence: confluence://lynwood-health/onboarding
- PR: github.com/redwood-inference/lynwood-integration-proto/pull/14

Raw action list (copyable):
- Asha: request/response examples (REST + JWT) — due 2026-06-18
- Mateo: KMS cross-account checklist + IAM policy — due 2026-06-19
- Priya: confirm control-plane redaction capabilities — due 2026-06-20
- Lynwood: provide 20 anonymized sample messages — due 2026-06-18
- Asha + Lynwood devs: run 20-sample eval, pick model family — due 2026-06-22
- Asha: create Confluence security brief + diagram — due 2026-06-21

Status: Draft notes; will update after internal infra check and after Lynwood provides samples.
